newsitem.title: FRANCE: Snecma no longer seeks Messier unit sale.
newsitem.headline: Snecma no longer seeks Messier unit sale.

text.p: French aero-engine maker Snecma no longer wants to sell its Messier-Bugatti aircraft brakes subsidiary, a Snecma spokesman said on Monday.
"Snecma does not want to divest itself of a subsidiary in which it has invested much in the last few years," he said, confirming reports in French newspapers.

In retaining Messier-Bugatti, the new chairman of state-owned Snecma, Jean-Paul Bechat, reverses a decision by predecessor, Bernard Dufour, whom he replaced in June and who wanted to focus Snecma on its core engines business and sell peripheral activities.
Snecma had been in talks with its subsidiary rocket-engine maker Societe Europeenne de Propulsion (SEP) ) and BF Goodrich for the sale of Messier-Bugatti, which specialises in carbon-fibre brakes.
The Messier-Bugatti sale would also have helped bring in extra revenues for Snecma and reduce its debt.
